title: Henselization of a pair
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring and $J\subseteq B$ an ideal. Let $\mathcal C$ be the category whose objects are the etale ring maps $B\to C$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] (i.e. $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ etale) such that the induced map $B/J\to C/JC$ is an isomorphism, and whose morphisms are the $B$-algebra maps. Then: (1) $\mathcal C$ is essentially small and directed (nonempty, any two objects map to a common one, any two parallel morphisms are coequalized by a morphism); (2) setting $B^h=\varinjlim_{C\in\mathcal C}C$ and $J^h=JB^h$, the pair $(B^h,J^h)$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]; (3) the map $B/J\to B^h/J^h$ is an isomorphism. (Stacks 0A02 also states that $(B,J)\mapsto(B^h,J^h)$ is left adjoint to the inclusion of henselian pairs into pairs; that clause is not used on the route and is not part of this node: dropped by the lead at review, 2026-10-09.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization) and its proof (directedness of $\mathcal C$, $A^h=\colim B$, $A/I=A^h/IA^h$); cited in this form in etale-cohomology.tex, proof of Lemma Tag 0A51

proof.text: *Notation; morphisms of $\mathcal C$; the canonical maps $\pi_C$.* Write $\bar B=B/J$. For an object $C$ of $\mathcal C$ the structure map induces a surjection $B\to\bar B\xrightarrow{\sim}C/JC$; let $\pi_C:C\to C/JC\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar B$ be the quotient map followed by the inverse isomorphism, a $B$-algebra map. Claim: for an object $C$ there is at most one $B$-algebra map $C\to\bar B$, namely $\pi_C$. Indeed a $B$-algebra map $\chi:C\to\bar B$ kills $JC$ (it is $B$-linear and $J\bar B=0$), so it factors through $C/JC$, and a $B$-algebra map out of $C/JC$ is determined on the image of $B$, which is everything. Consequently every morphism $\beta:C\to C'$ of $\mathcal C$ satisfies $\pi_{C'}\circ\beta=\pi_C$. Also every morphism of $\mathcal C$ is etale: $\operatorname{Spec}\beta$ is a morphism between schemes etale over $\operatorname{Spec}B$ commuting with the structure maps [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (3).

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization): implicit ('Since $B/IB=A/I$ for all objects $B$ of $\mathcal C$')

proof.text: *(1) $\mathcal C$ is essentially small; the colimit exists.* An etale $B$-algebra $C$ is of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism] (locally of finite presentation with affine source and target), so it is isomorphic to a quotient $B[x_1,\dots,x_n]/\mathfrak a$ by an ideal; equivalently, by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-etale-essentially-small-cover] applied to $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$, the affine etale $B$-schemes form an essentially small category. The objects of $\mathcal C$ whose ring is such a quotient form a set, and their full subcategory $\mathcal C_0$ is equivalent to $\mathcal C$ (the conditions 'etale' and '$\bar B\cong C/JC$' are invariant under $B$-algebra isomorphisms); colimits over $\mathcal C$ are computed over $\mathcal C_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory] (2). Filtered colimits of commutative $B$-algebras over a small filtered category exist (the filtered colimit of the underlying sets, operations computed at a common stage) [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise]. Once $\mathcal C$ is shown filtered (steps 3-4), $B^h=\varinjlim_{\mathcal C}C$ exists, with coprojections $\iota_C:C\to B^h$ (morphisms of $B$-algebras), and by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (1) it is also the colimit of the underlying diagram of rings. (Stacks leaves the set-theoretic point implicit; the same argument is step 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples].)

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization): '$A^h=\colim_{B\in\mathcal C}B$'; set-theoretic point not in Stacks, written by the agent as in literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex proof of Lemma Tag 04GW

proof.text: *(1) Nonempty; two objects map to a common one.* $B$ itself (identity) is an object: $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is the identity, an open immersion, hence etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1), and $\bar B\to B/J$ is the identity. Let $C,C'$ be objects and $C''=C\otimes_BC'$. $\operatorname{Spec}C''\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is etale as a base change of $B\to C'$ along $B\to C$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change], hence $\operatorname{Spec}C''\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is etale (composition, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (2)). Reduction modulo $J$: by associativity and commutativity of tensor products, $C''/JC''=C''\otimes_B\bar B\cong(C\otimes_B\bar B)\otimes_{\bar B}(C'\otimes_B\bar B)=(C/JC)\otimes_{\bar B}(C'/JC')$, and under this identification the map $\bar B\to C''/JC''$ is the tensor product of the isomorphisms $\bar B\to C/JC$, $\bar B\to C'/JC'$ over $\bar B$, so it is the isomorphism $\bar B\cong\bar B\otimes_{\bar B}\bar B\to(C/JC)\otimes_{\bar B}(C'/JC')$. So $C''$ is an object, and the coprojections $C\to C''$, $C'\to C''$ are $B$-algebra maps, i.e. morphisms of $\mathcal C$.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization): 'It is nonempty because $\mathrm{id}:A\to A$ is an object. If $B$ and $B'$ are two objects of $\mathcal C$, then $B''=B\otimes_AB'$ is an object of $\mathcal C$ (use Algebra, Lemma 00U2)'; the reduction mod $J$ is written out by the agent

proof.text: *(1) Parallel morphisms are coequalized; $\mathcal C$ is filtered.* Let $f,g:C\to C'$ be morphisms of $\mathcal C$. Put $E=C'\otimes_{f,C,g}C'$ and $D=E\otimes_{C'\otimes_BC'}C'$, formed with the natural surjection $C'\otimes_BC'\to E$ and the multiplication $\mu:C'\otimes_BC'\to C'$. Etaleness over $B$: $f$ is etale (step 1), so the right factor map $C'\to E$, the base change of $f$ along $g$, is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change] and $E$ is etale over $B$ (composition); $C'\otimes_BC'$ is etale over $B$ (step 3), so $\mu$ is etale (a map between $B$-algebras etale over $B$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (3)), so $E\to D$, its base change, is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change] and $D$ is etale over $B$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (2). Reduction modulo $J$ (written out by the agent; Stacks only states etaleness): base change $-\otimes_B\bar B$ commutes with the tensor products, so $D/JD\cong(\bar C'\otimes_{\bar f,\bar C,\bar g}\bar C')\otimes_{\bar C'\otimes_{\bar B}\bar C'}\bar C'$ with $\bar C=C/JC$, $\bar C'=C'/JC'$; the structure maps $\bar B\to\bar C$, $\bar B\to\bar C'$ are isomorphisms through which $\bar f,\bar g$ become $\mathrm{id}_{\bar B}$ ($B$-algebra maps $\bar B\to\bar B$, step 1), so $D/JD\cong(\bar B\otimes_{\bar B}\bar B)\otimes_{\bar B\otimes_{\bar B}\bar B}\bar B\cong\bar B$ and the structure map $\bar B\to D/JD$ is this isomorphism. So $D$ is an object. Let $c:C'\to D$ be the right-most factor map $a\mapsto1\otimes a$, a $B$-algebra map, hence a morphism. In $D$, $c(a)$ equals the image of $a\otimes1$ and of $1\otimes a\in C'\otimes_BC'$ (both map to $a$ under $\mu$); since $f(x)\otimes1=1\otimes g(x)$ in $E$ for $x\in C$, $c(f(x))=c(g(x))$, i.e. $c\circ f=c\circ g$. With step 3, $\mathcal C$ is filtered (Stacks 'directed', Categories Definition Tag 002V).

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization): 'Suppose that $f,g:B\to B'$ are two maps between objects of $\mathcal C$. Then a coequalizer is $(B'\otimes_{f,B,g}B')\otimes_{(B'\otimes_AB')}B'$ which is etale over $A$ by Algebra, Lemmas 00U2 and 00U7'

proof.text: *(3) $B/J\to B^h/J^h$ is an isomorphism.* By step 1 the maps $\pi_C:C\to\bar B$ form a cocone of $B$-algebra maps, so they induce a $B$-algebra map $\pi:B^h\to\bar B$ with $\pi\circ\iota_C=\pi_C$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. $\pi$ kills $J^h=JB^h$ ($B$-linear, $J\bar B=0$), so it induces $\bar\pi:B^h/J^h\to\bar B$; with $\theta:\bar B\to B^h/J^h$ the map induced by $B\to B^h$, $\bar\pi\circ\theta=\mathrm{id}_{\bar B}$ (a $B$-algebra map out of $\bar B$ is determined), so $\theta$ is injective. Surjectivity: every $x\in B^h$ is $\iota_C(c)$ for some object $C$ and $c\in C$ [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] (2); as $B\to C/JC$ is surjective, $c=b+y$ with $b\in B$, $y\in JC$, so $x=b\cdot1+\iota_C(y)$ with $\iota_C(y)\in JB^h$; thus $x\equiv b$ modulo $J^h$. Hence $\theta$ is an isomorphism of $B$-algebras with inverse $\bar\pi$. (Stacks: '$A^h/IA^h=\colim B/IB=\colim A/I=A/I$', i.e. reduction modulo $I$ commutes with colimits and the colimit of the constant diagram over the connected category $\mathcal C$ is $A/I$; the elementwise argument here proves the same.)

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization): 'Since $B/IB=A/I$ for all objects $B$ of $\mathcal C$ we see that $A^h/I^h=A^h/IA^h=\colim B/IB=\colim A/I=A/I$'

proof.text: *(2) Sections of etale $B^h$-algebras lift: the set-up.* We verify the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-lifting-henselian-pair] for $(B^h,J^h)$ (Stacks: condition (2) of Lemma 09XI). Let $B^h\to A'$ be a ring map with $\operatorname{Spec}A'\to\operatorname{Spec}B^h$ etale and $\sigma:A'\to B^h/J^h$ a $B^h$-algebra map. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-filtered-colimit-descent] (applied to the filtered colimit of rings $B^h=\varinjlim_{\mathcal C}C$, step 2) there are an object $C$, a ring map $C\to C'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C'\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ etale and an isomorphism of $B^h$-algebras $A'\cong C'\otimes_CB^h$ (via $\iota_C$); identify $A'$ with $C'\otimes_CB^h$. Let $s:C'\to\bar B$ be the composite $C'\to A'\xrightarrow{\sigma}B^h/J^h\xrightarrow{\bar\pi}\bar B$ (step 5). It is a $C$-algebra map for the $C$-algebra structure $\pi_C$ on $\bar B$ (because $\sigma$ is $B^h$-linear and $\bar\pi\circ(B^h\to B^h/J^h)\circ\iota_C=\pi\circ\iota_C=\pi_C$), in particular a $B$-algebra map.

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization): 'suppose given an etale ring map $A^h\to A'$ and $A^h$-algebra map $\sigma:A'\to A^h/I^h$. Then there exists a $B\in\mathcal C$ and an etale ring map $B\to B'$ such that $A'=B'\otimes_BA^h$. See Algebra, Lemma 00U2. Since $A^h/I^h=A/I$, the map $\sigma$ induces an $A$-algebra map $s:B'\to A/I$'

proof.text: *(2) The object $C'_g$.* $C'/JC'=C'\otimes_C(C/JC)$ is etale over $C/JC$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change], and $C/JC\cong\bar B$; $s$ kills $JC'$ and induces a $\bar B$-algebra map $\bar s:C'/JC'\to\bar B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-idempotent-splitting] (with $R=\bar B$, $S=C'/JC'$) there is an idempotent $\bar e\in C'/JC'$ with $\bar s(\bar e)=1$ such that $\bar s$ induces an isomorphism $(C'/JC')_{\bar e}\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar B$ (Stacks: '$B'/IB'=A/I\times C$ ... let $g\in B'$ map to $(1,0)$'). Choose $g\in C'$ lifting $\bar e$. Then $\operatorname{Spec}C'_g\to\operatorname{Spec}C'$ is an open immersion, so $C'_g$ is etale over $C'$, over $C$ and over $B$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1),(2); and $C'_g/JC'_g=(C'/JC')_{\bar e}$ (localization commutes with quotients), so the composite $\bar B\to C'_g/JC'_g\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar B$ (the second map induced by $\bar s$) is a $B$-algebra map $\bar B\to\bar B$, i.e. the identity, and $\bar B\to C'_g/JC'_g$ is an isomorphism. So $C'_g$ is an object of $\mathcal C$, and the structure map $C\to C'\to C'_g$ is a $B$-algebra map, i.e. a morphism $C\to C'_g$ of $\mathcal C$; hence $\iota_{C'_g}\circ(C\to C'_g)=\iota_C$ (cocone).

source.place: proof of Lemma Tag 0A02 (lemma-henselization): 'Then $B'/IB'=A/I\times C$ as $A/I$-algebra, where $C$ is the kernel of the map $B'/IB'\to A/I$ induced by $s$. Let $g\in B'$ map to $(1,0)\in A/I\times C$. Then $B\to B'_g$ is etale and $A/I\to B'_g/IB'_g$ is an isomorphism, i.e., $B'_g$ is an object of $\mathcal C$'

proof.text: *(2) The lift; conclusion that $(B^h,J^h)$ is henselian.* Let $\lambda:C'\to C'_g$ be the localization map. The ring maps $\iota_{C'_g}\circ\lambda:C'\to B^h$ and $\mathrm{id}:B^h\to B^h$ agree on $C$ (step 7: both restrict to $\iota_C$), so by the universal property of $C'\otimes_CB^h$ (the coproduct of commutative $C$-algebras) they induce a $B^h$-algebra map $\tau:A'=C'\otimes_CB^h\to B^h$, $c'\otimes x\mapsto\iota_{C'_g}(\lambda(c'))x$. It lifts $\sigma$: the two $B^h$-algebra maps $q\circ\tau$ and $\sigma$ from $A'$ to $B^h/J^h$ ($q$ the quotient map) agree iff they agree on $C'$; composing with the isomorphism $\bar\pi$ (step 5), on $C'$ the first is $\pi\circ\iota_{C'_g}\circ\lambda=\pi_{C'_g}\circ\lambda$ and the second is $s$. Now $s(g)=\bar s(\bar e)=1$, so $s$ extends to a $B$-algebra map $s_g:C'_g\to\bar B$ with $s_g\circ\lambda=s$; by step 1 (applied to the object $C'_g$) $s_g=\pi_{C'_g}$. Hence $\pi_{C'_g}\circ\lambda=s$ and $q\circ\tau=\sigma$ (Stacks: the two commutative diagrams). So $(B^h,J^h)$ satisfies the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-lifting-henselian-pair], hence $J^h$ lies in the Jacobson radical of $B^h$ and $(B^h,J^h)$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]: clause (2).
